name: Neon
summary: Neon is a fully managed Postgres database that automatically pauses itself when nobody is using it, so you only pay for active use.

free_plan_covers.note: Free plan: 0.5 GB storage and 100 compute hours a month, with the database auto-suspending after 5 minutes idle.

first_paid_usd_month.note: Paid plans are pure pay-as-you-go, metered hourly for compute and storage, with no flat monthly base fee or minimum.

portability.note: It is standard, wire-compatible Postgres, so you can dump and restore to any other Postgres host.

storage_model.note: Neon runs and manages the Postgres server for you in the cloud; there is no local-file option.

data_model.note: Neon is Postgres, a standard SQL relational database.

realtime_built_in.note: Neon offers logical replication to external systems, but nothing that pushes changes directly to a browser without extra work.

serverless_friendly.note: A built-in HTTP driver and a pooled connection string (via PgBouncer) support many concurrent serverless connections.

mobile_sdk.note: There is only a JavaScript/TypeScript SDK and raw HTTP access; no official Swift, Kotlin, or Flutter SDK for native apps.

setup.step: Create a free Neon account and a new project in the Neon Console.
Install the Neon serverless driver with npm install @neondatabase/serverless, or use any standard Postgres driver.
On the project dashboard, click Connect and copy the pooled connection string.
Add the connection string to your environment file.
Import the driver, connect using the environment variable, and run queries.

builder_notes: Use the pooled connection string (the '-pooler' host) in serverless or edge functions; use the direct string only for migrations.
Never expose DATABASE_URL in client-side code or in a variable the browser can read, since it contains the database password.
Use the @neondatabase/serverless package for edge-friendly HTTP queries, or a standard pg client in a long-running Node server.
